capabilities: Preview a local WXR XML export with post, page, and skip counts before importing
Create one Markdown note per post or page with source ID, dates, categories, and tags as properties
Append approved comments under a heading in each imported note
Generate an index note linking imported notes and a report of skipped records and shortcodes
Compare a later export against a stored snapshot to review added, changed, or removed posts (Pro)
disambiguation: Not a WordPress publishing or syncing tool; it only converts an XML export file into notes and never contacts a WordPress site.
extras: Freemium: free import covers posts, pages, comments, index, and report; folder/field mapping profiles and later-export comparison require Pro via GitHub Sponsors. After updates the plugin opens a What's new tab suggesting other NoteMods plugins and Zovo Chat (can be turned off). README lists untested areas (phones, live site exports, non-UTF-8 files, large archives).
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to turn a WordPress XML blog export into dated, tagged vault notes.

relations.evidence: WordPress WXR Import turns a local WordPress XML export into Markdown notes.

requires.name: GitHub Sponsors sponsorship of theluckystrike ($5/month or $15 once) for Pro features

summary: Importer that converts a local WordPress WXR XML export into Markdown notes with properties, approved comments, an index, and a skipped-record report.
